steps.message:
`routes/users.js:6` is the only place `userId` appears. Renaming it changes the `GET /users` response contract, and the repo's README names the consumers and the policy:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

So this isn't an internal rename — it's a breaking change for three consumers, including a shipped iOS app you can't update in lockstep and a partner export. The repo already says changes like this go through a versioned endpoint.

Before I touch it, I need your call on how to proceed.

questions.question: Renaming userId to user_id breaks GET /users for the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export. How should I handle it?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside the existing userId so consumers migrate on their own schedule, then drop userId later. Non-breaking, but the response carries a duplicate field until cleanup.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README policy: keep /users as-is and expose the snake_case shape on a new version (e.g. /v2/users). Most work, but no consumer breaks.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Do exactly what you asked: change userId to user_id in routes/users.js and nothing else. Breaks the three consumers the moment it deploys.
